location: Space Weather 9 S07002, doi:10.1029/2010SW000641; abstract; paras 16,22,39-40

title: McMahon-Crabtree et al., Automated characterization techniques and testbeds for event-based cameras
finding: PPS3MVCD and DAVIS346 (180 nm) showed dose-dependent background activity and functional issues above about 30 krad. One DAVIS346 failed at 50 krad after 20 krad step. A proton-exposed DAVIS346 recovered after rest/power cycle. At 20 krad proton exposure, dark current rose about 70% and dark event noise 23% (filter off).
conditions: PPS3MVCD Co 60 dose rate 52.1 rad(Si)/s, multiple devices. DAVIS346 gamma 4.23 rad(Si)/s; separate 64 MeV proton test reaches 1.498e11 p/cm 2 at 20 krad. Targeted irradiation; packaged-camera support circuitry can confound attribution.
limits: Cross-technology and sample-limited comparator, not IMX636 tolerance. Proton test combines TID and DD; no isolated DD coefficient or flight-rate cross-section. High dose-rate results do not bound all low-dose-rate/annealing effects.
access: author-uploaded full text read on ResearchGate; PDF download403; exact table tokens recorded, no local PDF visual check
